card: This PR prevents removeForReorg from erroneously evicting valid BIP68 transactions with unconfirmed parents when a chain reorganization lowers the chain tip. Previously, cached lockpoints based on the higher previous tip caused sequence locks to appear unsatisfied, leading to premature eviction of transactions and their descendants. The change recalculates lockpoints via CalculateLockPointsAtTip whenever cached sequence checks fail, evicting only if fresh lockpoints are truly unsatisfied. A functional test added to feature_bip68_sequence.py covers height-based, mixed confirmed/unconfirmed, and MTP-lowering time-based locks.
changed_since_previous: The implementation approach is unchanged; the test suite was expanded with test_reorg_unsatisfied_lock_evicted to verify that genuinely unsatisfied relative locks are still evicted after reorgs.
evidence: Closes issue #35007: 'removeForReorg incorrectly evicts valid BIP68 transactions with mempool parents after invalidateblock'.
Author provided a reproducer script demonstrating that valid transactions were evicted on unpatched nodes across an invalidateblock call.
Functional tests in feature_bip68_sequence.py demonstrate failures on master for unconfirmed, mixed-input, and time-based relative lock cases across reorgs.
problem: When a chain reorganization lowers the chain tip or median time past, valid BIP68 transactions spending unconfirmed inputs can be erroneously evicted from the mempool along with their descendants. Because their lockpoints were cached assuming confirmation at the old tip plus one, they fail sequence lock checks at the lower tip even though TestLockPointValidity still passes.

risk.why: A flaw in mempool reorg validation could improperly retain non-final transactions in the mempool or evict valid transactions during chain reorganizations.

summary: Recalculates BIP68 lockpoints during mempool reorg processing whenever cached lockpoints fail sequence-lock checks at the new chain tip. Previously, transactions with cached lockpoints that still passed validity checks were evicted immediately if their sequence locks failed against the new tip. With this change, the mempool only evicts if newly recalculated lockpoints at the new tip also fail sequence verification.
